title: carrier-connectivity-aware observation code allocation
hypothesis: When the most reliable private sensor is disconnected from the aggregator, a connectivity-aware task code can choose a reachable carrier for each query and preserve inference quality with fewer transmitted observations than broad central collection.
physical_object: Eight private sensor agents arranged as two carriers for each of four latent coordinates, plus aggregator and relay links
mirror_coordinate: One uint8 agent address per coordinate query, paired with a topology/reliability schema
logical_multiplicity: Four coordinate-query functions served by one connected submesh and a small task address table
controls: central posterior from all reachable carriers
native graph/reliability rule versus Mirror address table

development.selection_metric: no tuning; fixed line topology and fixed cut probability

world.agents: 8; two private noisy carriers per coordinate
world.topology: aggregator connects to sensor 0, sensors form a chain; edge between sensors 3 and 4 is independently cut with probability .5
world.noise: per coordinate, one near/far sensor has sigma=.25 and the other sigma=.75, assigned by fresh seed
world.observation: agent id, typed coordinate id, one float32 value only; relays forward the unchanged typed observation

policy.query_budget: one admitted carrier per coordinate query
policy.connectivity_rule: choose minimum-noise sensor among those with a path to aggregator
policy.quality: posterior normalized MSE; unreachable required carriers yield prior error 1
policy.message_accounting: count each hop transmission of each admitted observation, including relays

storage.authority: actual serialized topology/reliability schema and policy bytes
storage.message: uint8 agent ID + uint8 type ID + float32 value = 6 bytes

success_gate: For all fresh worlds, connectivity-aware code has mean nMSE within .02 of reachable-central posterior, uses fewer message-hop bytes than central, and never selects a disconnected sensor; Mirror-specific gain requires outperforming native connectivity/reliability routing.
failure_gate: Any connectivity violation, quality miss, no message-hop reduction, or exact alias with native routing fails Mirror-specific attribution. Report the connectivity utility independently.
boundaries: Synthetic scalar linear-Gaussian system only; no neural network or arbitrary Mesh topology claim.
Only a line with one possible cut is tested; higher-dimensional graph routing is untested.
Only observations are transmitted; private models, gradients, and hidden states remain local.
Policy addresses are not independent capacity units.
